---
title: "Appendix 1 — Comparision of Summary and Per Point DCA Curves"
date: last-modified
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dpi = 150)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(data.table); library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)})
HERE <- ".." # this .qmd lives in manuscript/; repo root is ..
for (f in list.files(file.path(HERE, "R"), "^fn_.*\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
```

**Situation** The summary route (reconstruct a decision curve from a model's reported PR-AUC via a binormal ROC) is cheap but assumes a curve shape. 
Wheras the per-point route (reweight the held-out predictions to the target prevalence) is exact but needs the raw predictions. 
Here we determine whether the two values disagree substantially. 

**Experiment.** For 128 SDMs of *E. coloradense* spanning presence:absence ratios from 1:1 to 1:30, we computed both decision curves at a target landscape prevalence and recorded their difference.
Defined as: `gap = net benefit (summary) − net benefit (exact)`, and averaged over a prevalence-relative threshold window. 
We then (i) held the target landscape prevalence at 2.5% and varied the P:A ratio. 
Additionally we (ii) swept the target prevalence from 1% to 50% to determine if this trend prevailed across ratios.
Each model's binormal was anchored to its own reported PR-AUC at its evaluation prevalence; the gap is a median across replicate seeds.

```{r ratio-sweep}
#| include: false
## (i) Fixed 2.5% target, gap vs P:A ratio and vs hold-out calibration.
## Per hold-out model (raw, classic excluded), at the landscape prevalence PI:
##   nb_exact()    -- net benefit thresholding the RAW probs, reweighted to PI (per-point,
##                    calibration-DEPENDENT: uses the model's actual cutoffs).
##   nb_binormal() -- net benefit from a binormal ROC fit to the model's PR-AUC, read at the
##                    ROC point whose slope matches the cost ratio (summary, calibration-
##                    INDEPENDENT best-achievable NB for that ROC).
## gap = summary - exact has two sources: (a) binormal shape, (b) raw-prob vs optimal cutoffs;
## (b) is why hold-out cox calibration is the natural covariate to test (not a claim).
PI   <- 0.025
PT   <- seq(0.005, 0.25, by = 0.005)              # decision-relevant threshold range for the gap
GRID <- 3000                                      # binormal integration grid

d <- fread(file.path(HERE, "data", "holdout_point_predictions.csv"))
d <- d[calibration == "raw" & design == "spatial_mapping"]
d <- d[!(seed %in% c(5001, 5002, 5003))] # drop the 3-seed replicate; keep 5101-5801 reps
d[, pa_ratio := as.numeric(sub(".*PA1:([0-9.]+)DO.*", "\\1", model))]

res <- d[, {
  if (uniqueN(Presence) < 2 || .N < 30) .SD[0] # need both classes and a usable n
  else {
    pih <- mean(Presence); pr <- ap_pointwise(Presence, prob, pih)
    mu  <- tryCatch(uniroot(function(m) ap_binormal(m, pih, grid = GRID) - pr, c(1e-3, 8))$root,
                    error = function(e) NA_real_)
    gap <- if (is.na(mu)) rep(NA_real_, length(PT)) else nb_binormal(mu, PI, PT) - nb_exact(Presence, prob, PI, PT)
    cc  <- cox_calibration(Presence, prob)
    data.table(design = design[1], resolution = resolution[1], pa_ratio = pa_ratio[1],
               n = .N, prev_holdout = pih, pr_auc = pr, mu = mu,
               cox_intercept = cc[["cox_intercept"]], cox_slope = cc[["cox_slope"]],
               gap_mean = mean(gap), gap_absmean = mean(abs(gap)))   # gap = binormal - exact
  }
}, by = model]
fwrite(res, file.path(HERE, "data", "binormal_vs_exact_sweep.csv"))

n_models <- nrow(res)
spear_cox <- cor(res$cox_intercept, res$gap_mean, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

## exploratory views: does the (signed) gap track P:A ratio or hold-out calibration?
plot_gap <- function(xvar, xlab) {
  ggplot(res, aes(.data[[xvar]], gap_mean, size = n)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5, colour = cda_cols[["sweep_point"]]) +
    geom_smooth(aes(weight = n), method = "loess", se = TRUE, colour = cda_cols[["sweep_trend"]], linewidth = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Mean net-benefit gap  (summary - exact)",
         title = sprintf("Summary-vs-exact decision-curve gap at %.1f%% prevalence", 100 * PI),
         subtitle = "Exploratory, one point per hold-out model; point size = hold-out n. Above 0 = summary route optimistic.") +
    theme_cda()
}
p_ratio <- plot_gap("pa_ratio", "Training P:A ratio (1 : x)") + scale_x_log10()
p_cox   <- plot_gap("cox_intercept", "Hold-out cox calibration intercept (0 = calibrated-in-the-large)")
ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "sweep_gap_vs_ratio.png"), p_ratio, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 150)
ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "sweep_gap_vs_cox.png"),   p_cox,   width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

**Result.** The discord, between the two methods to calculate DCA, is governed by the distance between a model's *evaluation* prevalence (set by its P:A ratio, natural prevalence $1/(1+\text{ratio})$) and the *target* prevalence.
The model's calibration has no effect (hold-out cox intercept, Spearman $\approx `r sprintf("%.2f", spear_cox)`$).

```{r}
#| label: fig-gap-ratio
#| fig-cap: "At a fixed 2.5% target, the summary route is optimistically biased for models evaluated at balanced ratios and converges on the exact curve as the design ratio approaches landscape rarity."
p_ratio
```

```{r target-sweep}
#| include: false
## (ii) Falsification test: sweep the TARGET prevalence; each P:A ratio's gap should bottom out
## where the target equals that ratio's natural evaluation prevalence 1/(1+ratio). Strong form:
## rescale x to target / natural prevalence and every ratio collapses onto one curve crossing 0 at 1.
GRID <- 3000

## mean gap over a prevalence-RELATIVE threshold window (same relative tolerance at every target)
mean_gap <- function(truth, prob, mu, pi_target) {
  pt <- pmin(pi_target * seq(0.25, 10, by = 0.25), 0.95)
  mean(nb_binormal(mu, pi_target, pt) - nb_exact(truth, prob, pi_target, pt))
}

g <- fread(file.path(HERE, "data", "holdout_point_predictions.csv"))
g <- g[calibration == "raw" & design == "spatial_mapping"]
g <- g[!(seed %in% c(5001, 5002, 5003))]
g[, pa_ratio := round(as.numeric(sub(".*PA1:([0-9.]+)DO.*", "\\1", model)))]  # collapse ~1:1 cluster to 1

## fit mu once per model (anchored at its own evaluation prevalence + PR-AUC)
mods <- g[, {
  if (uniqueN(Presence) < 2 || .N < 30) .SD[0] else {
    pih <- mean(Presence); pr <- ap_pointwise(Presence, prob, pih)
    mu  <- tryCatch(uniroot(function(m) ap_binormal(m, pih, grid = GRID) - pr, c(1e-3, 8))$root, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    .(pa_ratio = pa_ratio[1], eval_prev = pih, mu = mu)
  }
}, by = model]
pt_list <- split(g[, .(Presence, prob)], g$model)

targets <- 10^seq(log10(0.01), log10(0.50), length.out = 13)
long <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mods)), function(i) {
  mm <- mods[i]; if (is.na(mm$mu)) return(NULL)
  pp <- pt_list[[mm$model]]
  data.table(model = mm$model, pa_ratio = mm$pa_ratio, eval_prev = mm$eval_prev,
             target_prev = targets,
             gap = vapply(targets, function(tp) mean_gap(pp$Presence, pp$prob, mm$mu, tp), numeric(1)))
}))
long[, nat_prev := 1 / (1 + pa_ratio)]
agg <- long[, .(gap = median(gap), n = .N), by = .(pa_ratio, nat_prev, target_prev)]
fwrite(agg, file.path(HERE, "data", "gap_vs_target_prevalence.csv"))

## Fig A: gap vs target prevalence, one line per ratio; dots mark each ratio's natural prevalence
markA <- long[, .(target_prev = nat_prev[1], gap = median(gap[which.min(abs(target_prev - nat_prev))])),
              by = pa_ratio]
p_target <- ggplot(agg, aes(target_prev, gap, colour = nat_prev, group = pa_ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = markA, aes(target_prev, gap), colour = "black", size = 1.3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_colour_ratio() +
  labs(x = "Target landscape prevalence", y = "Median net-benefit gap (summary - exact)",
       title = "Each P:A ratio's gap bottoms out at its own evaluation prevalence",
       subtitle = "Dots = each ratio's natural prevalence 1/(1+ratio). Above 0 = summary route optimistic.") +
  theme_cda()
ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "gap_vs_target_prevalence.png"), p_target, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)

## Fig B: strong form -- rescale x to target / natural prevalence; curves collapse, cross 0 at 1
p_collapse <- ggplot(agg, aes(target_prev / nat_prev, gap, colour = nat_prev, group = pa_ratio)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_ratio() +
  labs(x = "Target prevalence / evaluation prevalence", y = "Median net-benefit gap (summary - exact)",
       title = "Collapse test: the gap is a function of target / evaluation prevalence",
       subtitle = "If the mechanism holds, every ratio falls on one curve crossing 0 at x = 1 (dotted).") +
  theme_cda()
ggsave(file.path(HERE, "figures", "gap_collapse_test.png"), p_collapse, width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 150)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-gap-target
#| fig-cap: "Sweeping the target prevalence, every ratio's gap bottoms out where the target equals that ratio's own evaluation prevalence (dots). Flip the target to 50% and balanced models thrive while rare-tuned models suffer — the mirror of the 2.5% case."
p_target
```

**Conclusion** 
When, the model was trained on a presence:absence ratio that differs vastly from the landscape prevalence of the taxon (e.g. 1:1), use the per-point calculation for DCAs..
